reading.body:
Oregon's legislature addressed artificial intelligence in two bills during 2026: one governing AI systems broadly and one specific to AI companions, neither directly constraining compute or power infrastructure.

HB4103 and SB1546 represent Oregon's regulatory approach to AI, filed in early March and April respectively. The bills target different aspects of the technology: one addresses artificial intelligence generally, while the other focuses specifically on AI companions. Neither bill title indicates restrictions on data center construction, power consumption, or compute allocation. The broader legislative context shows Oregon handled emergency measures on housing, elections, and public safety in the same session, suggesting AI regulation occurred within routine legislative activity rather than as an urgent state priority.

The data does not reveal the bills' actual provisions, thresholds, or enforcement mechanisms. It does not show whether Oregon's AI legislation imposed operational constraints on model training, energy use, or facility siting. Without access to bill text or status records, it is unclear whether either measure passed, was signed into law, or remains pending. A reader seeking to understand Oregon's role in the compute-constrained AI landscape would need to examine the bills themselves.
